name: 1827 Prairie Avenue — the John W. Doane house (K01; refined by T-3172, T-1896)

grade.why: Pictured: 3 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the photograph (undated, after the house's completion in 1882) shows the same main block. Its building and loss dates are not read here.

placement.position_note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body, the draft's own origin (lot frame u 15.000, v -10.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own check, 1.47 m RMS, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.449 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line; v runs SOUTH, from the north wall toward 1829.
placement.symbolic_location: 1827 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1827 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1827-b1 p2) in the house's frame: its west (Prairie) front at u 24.4-24.5 (the wall behind the porch and south of the pavilion), its north wall at v 0 (the trace at v -0.1), its south wall at v 15.5 (the trace at 15.46-15.71) and its east wall at u 0. The porch, the pavilion and the rear range stand on it; the rear part's 1.2 m and 1.6 m steps out on the north and south flanks (u 0-14.6) are not built (the match record); the corner feature at the south-west corner is the corner tower (bays, T-3176).

stories.note: Two full storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, as the photograph shows on the front and the south flank; the sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey (as it does at 1729, 1801 and 1816).

construction.note: '3B stone with brick rear' on the 1911 sheet; the photograph shows coursed ashlar on the Prairie front and the south flank alike. The brick rear is the rear range (rear_wings).

stone_front.note: RECONSTRUCTED as to the stone: the print is monochrome and shows a light ashlar with darker courses between lighter ones; Lemont limestone, K02's light Chicago stone, stands for it. Laid in smooth courses over a two-course base to the basement lights' heads. The alternating course heights the photograph shows are not laid (open in the match record).

principal_floor_m.note: T-3189: read through the photograph's camera (data/reference_views/doane_house_1827_prairie/chicagology_doane_exterior.json) as T-3176 re-solved it on the 1911 sheet's plan: the water table's top over the raised basement stands at y 1452 px on the front beside the pavilion, grade there at y 1556-1561, about 1.3 m over grade (T-3171 had 2.0-2.2 m through a camera that stood on an assumed corner point and set the house about a third too tall). The pavilion's reads the same (y 1455 px, 1.24 m).

storey_heights_m.note: T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the string course between the storeys at y 1128 px on the front (about 5.3 m over grade; 5.1 m on the pavilion's face), and the main cornice's top at y 790 px (about 9.4 m; 9.5 m on the pavilion), over a frieze and bed moulding at y 855 px (8.6 m) above the second storey's heads. So 4.0 and 4.1 m over the 1.3 m water table; T-3171's 5.5 and 5.1 m put the cornice at 12.6 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a dressed-stone front's thickness inside the contract's masonry range (0.23-0.45 m), taken at its top for a three-storey stone house; no source gives it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: as the front's; no source gives it.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the common brick K01 lays for the sheet's brick rear range; no picture sees the rear.

street_front_trim.note: Plain stone lintels stand in for the photograph's window heads: the segmental hoods over the front's windows and the carved hoods over the pavilion's centre lights (open in the match record).

wall_head.note: The photograph's deep moulded stone cornice, run round the front and the south flank and on round the walls it does not see.

roof_form.note: The photograph's steep slated faces over the cornice, with dormers on the front: a mansard.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the deck over the curb, which no picture sees, inside K05's mansard_upper range.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the cornice's projection, taken at K01's ordinary value; the photograph shows a deep cornice but its depth is not measured through the camera.

mansard.note: T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the slated lower faces rise steeply from the cornice (about 9.4 m) to the curb, its crest at y 553 px over the window bay south of the pavilion (about 12.3 m), a rise of about 2.9 m; a dormer under a pediment stands on the front over that bay (x 650-770 px, its light from about 9.6 to 11.1 m, y 775-655, its peak at the curb, so it stands 0.05 m up the face rather than 0.1) and another over the porch at the north end (x 190-250 px). The pavilion's crown (T-3175), read the same way: the pavilion carried up an attic from the main eave to its own cornice at about y 588 px on its face (about 12.1 m, the main curb's height; attic_m 2.9), under a steep slated roof hipped on every side from that cornice (x 350-597 px) to a point at about y 407 px (about 15.1 m) with a turned iron finial to about y 352 px (about 0.8-1 m). Built as K05's hipped crown at 47 degrees on the sides and the street end, the nearest the kit's steep range (over 45) allows: the print's rise of about 3.0 m over a half-width of about 3.4 m reads 41 degrees, so the build's point stands about 0.7 m over the print's (open in the match record). The cornice 0.65 m past the pavilion's face and sides (the kit's least past the main cornice's 0.6 m), run 6.0 m back into the main roof so its ridge is short (the photograph sees it end on, as a point). How far it runs back, which no picture shows, is reconstructed.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the lower faces, as the photograph's coursed grey faces read; the deck over the curb is not seen and is reconstructed as tin.

stair_tread_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: inside the contract's stair range; no source gives the treads.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The sheet's stone range at the front's north end, 2.7 m deep in front of the west wall (s28fp-1827-b1 p1, u 24.4-27.2), read as the porch the photograph shows there: its floor is the landing the columns stand on.

stoop_width_m.note: The porch's floor, as wide as the sheet's range (v 0.05-5.05); the flight is laid across it, where the photograph shows steps rising along the front from the north behind the street tree (open in the match record).

entrance_bay.note: The door stands in the Prairie front's north bay (K01's 'south' end is v 0, the north wall, in this house's frame), under the porch the sheet draws over v 0-5.05; the photograph shows the porch's columns, arches and balcony at the front's north end, behind the street tree.

front_bays.note: Along the Prairie front from the north wall: the door's bay under the porch (v 2.55, the porch's centre) and the window bay south of the pavilion (v 12.9; x 665-745 px, one window a storey under a segmental hood). The pavilion's own lights are the K08 projection's.

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the north flank's windows, which no picture sees; 1823 stands 3 m north of it.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED as to their places: the south flank's windows behind the corner, counted from the Prairie corner; the photograph shows windows on this flank (x 1180-1240 px) but sees it too obliquely, and behind a tree, to place them.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the east wall's window beside the rear range, which no picture sees.

sash_by_storey.note: T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the front's principal-storey window beside the pavilion from about 1.6 to 4.3 m over grade (sill y 1432 px, head y 1210) and the second storey's from about 5.6 to 8.0 m (y 1105 and 910 px), each about 1.15 m wide (K01's widest sash, 1.15 m; 77 px through the camera at the front's angle, the print's 80 px with its frame).

basement_lights.note: The raised basement's barred lights under the front's windows (x 290-370 and 565-650 px). T-3189: through the re-solved camera the print's run from about grade to about 1.0 m (y 1475-1553 px beside the pavilion), under the 1.3 m water table; K02's two base courses hold the build's to 0.3-1.05 m, within about 0.2 m of them.

chimneys.note: Two tall stone stacks with moulded caps stand over the south flank behind the corner in the photograph (x 1240-1300 px); their places along the flank are not read through the camera and are reconstructed.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: one copper downpipe on the rear wall; none is read off the photograph.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two-over-two sash; the photograph shows one-over-one and two-light sash behind blinds, which the kit's pattern stands for.

entrance_kit.note: The sheet's stone range at the front's north end (u 24.4-27.2, v 0.05-5.05) is the porch the photograph shows there behind the street tree: columns carrying a balustraded balcony at the second floor, built as the door's hood on columns with a railing over it. T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the entablature's foot at y 1175 px at the porch's south side (about 4.85 m over grade), its balcony's railing over it to y 1130 (about 5.4 m), its floor on the columns' bases at about y 1422 (about 1.6 m). Built with its soffit at 4.7 m, a 0.2 m fascia, a 0.12 m cornice and a 0.45 m railing (to about 5.5 m), so the balcony stops under the second storey's sills over the door's bay, which the kit will not stand a railing in front of; the print's entablature reads about 0.2 m and its railing about 0.45-0.5 m. Its round arches are not built (open in the match record).

boundary.note: The photograph's low iron fence of scrolled bars on a stone curb along the Prairie Avenue line (y 1630-1700 px), ending at a stone pier south of the house (x 1165-1200 px), where the walk turns back along the south flank: K11's scroll-band fence; the side passage's gate at the lot's north end, beside 1823, which no picture sees, is reconstructed. The lot runs v -1.97 to 22.47 on the 1904 parcel.

the upper storey's lights: through the re-solved camera (T-3189) about 5.5 to 7.55 m over grade (y 1122 and 960 px), taller than the rules' ordinary sash

the attic's three tall lights, read off the Doane photograph through its re-solved camera (T-3175, T-3189): three lights about 40 px across at x 357-400, 413-457 and 463-500 px on the pavilion's face (269-601 px for its 5.46 m), about 0.7 m each, their sills just over the main cornice's top (y about 795 px, about 9.65 m) and their heads under the crown's cornice (y about 625 px, about 11.8 m), centred on the pavilion; the photograph's lights have arched transom heads, which the kit's flat transom stands for

the principal floor's tall lights, as the front's and the pavilion's: the photograph's paired lights in the corner tower's broad face (x 925-985 and 1010-1060 px) run nearly the storey's height, level with the front's (about 1.6 to 4.3 m over grade through the re-solved camera, T-3189)
the upper storey's lights, level with the front's and the pavilion's (the photograph's y 900-1090 px on the tower's broad face; about 5.6 to 8.0 m over grade through the re-solved camera, T-3189)

the tower stage's paired lights over the main cornice (the photograph's x 925-975 and 1005-1050, y 575-730 px), read through the re-solved camera on the tower's broad face (T-3189): about 9.7 to 11.5 m over grade

bays.note: The sheet's shallow pavilion on the front (u 24.4-24.97, v 5.33-10.79: 5.46 m wide, 0.47 m out), carried full height with the photograph's three lights a storey (x 330-530 px: a wide centre light between two narrow ones), and on up an attic storey past the main cornice to its own crown (T-3175): the Doane photograph shows the pavilion rising through the mansard, three tall lights in its attic wall (x 357-500 px), under a steep pyramidal roof of its own (mansard.crown). And the corner tower (T-3176): the sheet's corner feature at the south-west corner is a square turned 45 degrees across the corner, its north-west face meeting the front at v 14.36, its angles at u 25.5, v 15.5 and u 24.0, v 17.1 and its south-east face meeting the flank at u 22.3 (2.27 m on a face, centred on u 23.98, v 15.55); the photograph's broad south-west face (x 857-1135 px) is about 3.2 m, 3.5 times the front's 1.15 m window beside it, and the camera re-fitted with the square's side free on the sheet's centre puts it at 3.25 m (4.4 px RMS; the sheet's own 2.27 m leaves 40-47 px). Built as K08's polygonal tower turned 45 degrees across the front's south corner (s_m 15.5, its centre 0.42 m inside the front and on the flank's plane, radius 2.298 m), its walls on the three faces outside the house: one light a storey on the north-west face and a pair on the south-west, read off the print, and a pair on the unseen south-east face, reconstructed. T-3189: its heights read through the re-solved camera on its broad face (grade at y 1576 px): the bands at the front's string course (5.3 m) and cornice (9.4 m), its wall top under the brackets at y 522 px (about 12.1 m), its cornice's top at y 448 (about 12.9 m), its eaves 0.45 m out, a slated hip at pitch 2.57 cut to a deck about 1.0 m across at about 16.5 m (y 175 px, over the tower's centre), an iron crest 0.6 m tall round the deck (y 140-175 px, to about 17.0 m) and a turned finial on each corner (the print shows the near two, y 88-130, to about 17.6 m). T-3176 had read them in proportion to T-3171's 12.6 m cornice, which put the deck at 22.0 m. What it does not carry (its bracketed cornice, its lights' hoods) is open on the match record.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's brick rear range behind the main body (s28fp-1827-b1 p3, u -3.8 to 0, v 0.85-11.6), two storeys under a flat tin deck; its windows, which no picture sees, are reconstructed. T-3189: its floor and storeys brought down with the main block's (1.3 m, and 3.6 and 3.7 m, so its deck stands about 1 m under the main cornice, as T-3171 set it); no picture sees it, so its heights are inferred from the main block's.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone with brick rear dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: 1827 S. Prairie [John W. Doane residence]. Unknown photographer, undated (after the house's completion in late 1882). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1827 S. the heights of the basement, the storeys, the windows, the cornice and the mansard through the photograph's camera
the corner block, its tower and the pavilion's pyramidal roof (T-3172), and the south flank's stacks
what_it_does_not_supply: the north flank, the rear and the brick rear range
the porch's detail and the door, behind the street tree

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: The John W. Doane house (1882, reported architect Theodore V. Wadskier), moved off the district draft onto K01 by T-3171 (piece 1 of T-1895) under the draft's own id: the 1911 sheet's main block in coursed stone, two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard with pedimented dormers, the shallow pavilion on the front, the porch at the front's north end (the sheet's stone range) and the brick rear range, read through the solved camera of the Chicagology photograph (undated, after 1882). The pavilion's pyramidal roof (T-3175) and the square tower turned across the south-west corner (T-3176) are T-3172's; T-3176 re-solved the photograph's camera on the tower. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1827-doane-3171/README.md.
